nodes.title: GraphQL testing branch
nodes.goal: Evaluate the exposed GraphQL surface using a structured, evidence-driven workflow covering endpoint identification, schema recovery, authorization validation, and query depth controls.
nodes.why: GraphQL endpoints combine multiple data models and operations into a single endpoint, where misconfigurations can expose the entire backend schema and bypass object-level access controls.
checklist: Confirm the GraphQL endpoint and establish a baseline benign query ('{ __typename }').
Determine introspection status and supported HTTP request methods (GET, POST with application/json, POST with application/graphql, x-www-form-urlencoded).
Map queries, mutations, and custom types to guide subsequent authorization and injection tests.
lookFor: Disclosed GraphQL endpoints, active introspection, detailed field-level error messages, and unauthenticated administrative operations.
nodes.record: Document tested endpoints, parameter values, observed responses, and evidence of validation behavior.
cautions: Verify testing scope and obtain explicit written authorization before testing; avoid destructive actions.

nodes.title: Identify GraphQL endpoint
nodes.goal: Locate all active GraphQL interfaces across standard and non-standard URL paths and HTTP methods.
nodes.why: GraphQL endpoints can expose schema detail and authorization gaps through a single flexible interface.
checklist: Probe common GraphQL path endpoints (/graphql, /api/graphql, /v1/graphql, /graphql.php, /api, /query, /v1/api).
Send probe queries using POST with Content-Type application/json payload '{"query": "{__typename}"}'.
Test alternative HTTP methods (GET query string '?query={__typename}', POST with URL-encoded parameters) if POST JSON is blocked.
Inspect client-side JavaScript bundle files for GraphQL client configurations (Apollo Client, Relay, Urql) disclosing backend query endpoints.
lookFor: HTTP 200 responses containing '{"data":{"__typename":"Query"}}' or syntax error responses containing GraphQL error structures ('{"errors":[{"message":...}]}').
nodes.record: Document tested endpoints, parameter values, observed responses, and evidence of validation behavior.
cautions: Verify testing scope and obtain explicit written authorization before testing; avoid destructive actions.

nodes.title: Test introspection
nodes.goal: Determine whether GraphQL schema introspection is enabled, allowing complete recovery of types, queries, mutations, and fields.
nodes.why: Introspection provides a full map of the backend data model and available API operations.
checklist: Submit standard introspection query ('{"query":"{__schema{types{name,fields{name}}}}"}') via POST and GET.
If full introspection is blocked, test partial schema discovery via field suggestions (e.g., submitting typo query '{ user { passwor } }' to trigger "Did you mean 'password'?" suggestions).
Test introspection bypasses (adding whitespace/newlines around '__schema', using aliases '{ test: __schema { types { name } } }', or switching from POST to GET).
Check for exposed GraphQL IDE interfaces (GraphQL Playground, GraphiQL, Altair) at paths like /graphql/playground, /graphiql, /altair.
lookFor: Complete schema responses returning all types and queries, informative field suggestions revealing hidden field names, and enabled interactive GraphiQL playgrounds.
nodes.record: Document tested endpoints, parameter values, observed responses, and evidence of validation behavior.
cautions: Verify testing scope and obtain explicit written authorization before testing; avoid destructive actions.

nodes.title: Enumerate schema
nodes.goal: Extract and analyze the full GraphQL schema to identify sensitive queries, administrative mutations, and hidden data fields.
nodes.why: Full schema extraction highlights high-value operations and hidden objects that lack authorization enforcement.
checklist: Dump the complete schema structure using introspection queries or tools like Clairvoyance and GraphQL Voyager.
Review all exposed Query operations for sensitive data retrieval (e.g., allUsers, systemLogs, paymentDetails, exportData).
Review all Mutation operations for state modification (e.g., updateUserRole, resetPassword, deleteAccount, uploadFile).
Inspect custom object types and scalar fields for private attributes (e.g., passwordHash, ssn, apiKey, internalId, role).
lookFor: Sensitive administrative queries, unadvertised mutations, exposed credential fields, and internal database object mappings.
nodes.record: Document tested endpoints, parameter values, observed responses, and evidence of validation behavior.
cautions: Verify testing scope and obtain explicit written authorization before testing; avoid destructive actions.

nodes.title: Test GraphQL authorization
nodes.goal: Verify that individual GraphQL queries, mutations, and nested fields enforce object-level and role-based authorization.
nodes.why: Field-level resolvers often lack individual permission checks, permitting unauthorized access to sensitive relationships.
checklist: Execute administrative queries (e.g., 'query { users { id username email role } }') with an unauthenticated or low-privilege token.
Test IDOR on parameterized queries (e.g., 'query { user(id: 1) { email privateNotes } }' vs 'id: 2').
Test mutations modifying other users' resources (e.g., 'mutation { updateUser(id: 1, role: "admin") { success } }').
Test nested field authorization where top-level object is authorized but nested relationships leak restricted data (e.g., 'query { myProfile { organization { allMembers { salary } } } }').
lookFor: Unauthorized data disclosure via unauthenticated queries, IDOR in query parameters, privilege escalation via mutations (as in HTB Passman), and authorization gaps in nested resolvers.
nodes.record: Document tested endpoints, parameter values, observed responses, and evidence of validation behavior.
cautions: Verify testing scope and obtain explicit written authorization before testing; avoid destructive actions.

nodes.title: Test query depth and mutations
nodes.goal: Assess protections against Denial of Service (DoS) through recursive circular queries, batching attacks, and injection within resolvers.
nodes.why: Unbounded GraphQL query depth and batching allow denial of service and rapid brute-force attacks through single HTTP requests.
checklist: Test deeply nested circular queries (e.g., 'query { author { posts { author { posts { author { name } } } } } }') to verify query depth limiting.
Test query batching and aliasing attacks (submitting multiple aliased queries 'a1: user(id:1), a2: user(id:2)' in a single request) to bypass rate limiting and brute-force passwords/tokens.
Test SQL injection, NoSQL injection, and command injection inside GraphQL query arguments and filter variables.
Test request size limits and maximum field cost analysis.
lookFor: Server timeouts or 500 errors from deep circular queries, successful password brute-forcing via query aliasing/batching, and resolver-level injection vulnerabilities.
